props.gloss_en: Rav Pappa: a pig's mouth is like passing feces
[it is like passing feces] even though it has come up from the river
doubtful feces -- [reading the Shema before it] is forbidden
doubtful urine -- [reading the Shema before it] is permitted
doubtful feces in the house -- permitted
doubtful feces on the dung-heap -- forbidden
doubtful urine -- even on the dung-heap, permitted
Rav Hamnuna: the Torah forbade [urine] only opposite the stream

R' Yonatan set 'you shall have a place outside the camp and go out there' (Deut 23:13) against 'you shall have a spade... and cover your excrement' (Deut 23:14), and resolved: the verse of covering speaks of feces
R' Yonatan: the verse without covering speaks of urine
hence: urine the Torah forbade only opposite the stream; once it has fallen to the ground it is permitted
and it is the Rabbis who decreed on [urine on the ground]
and when the Rabbis decreed, it was on the certain case; on the doubtful case they did not decree
[certain urine forbids] as long as it moistens
Geniva in Rav's name: [certain urine forbids] as long as its mark is visible
Rav (via Rav Yehuda): feces, once its surface has crusted -- permitted
feces, even [dry] like earthenware -- forbidden
R' Yochanan (via Rabba bar bar Chana): [it is like earthenware] as long as, when thrown, it does not crumble
some say: as long as, when rolled, it does not crumble
Rav Yehuda of Difti (as Ravina reports): examine whether its surface has crusted or not
some say he told him: examine whether it is cracked
Mar Zutra: feces like earthenware -- permitted
the baraita: urine, as long as it moistens, forbids; absorbed or dried -- permitted
a vessel from which urine was poured -- it is forbidden to read the Shema opposite it
the poured urine itself: absorbed -- permitted; not absorbed -- forbidden
R' Yosei: [it forbids] as long as it moistens
(entertained) the amoraic dispute over how long urine forbids is the tannaitic dispute of the tanna kama and R' Yosei
(entertained) for the tanna kama, 'absorbed' means it no longer moistens, 'not absorbed' that it moistens
then R' Yosei's position would simply BE the tanna kama's
(inside the leima) rather, 'absorbed' means its mark is not visible and 'not absorbed' that it is; R' Yosei came to say a visible mark permits
no: all agree that it forbids as long as it moistens, and a visible mark permits
and here the difference between them is [urine] moist enough to moisten

objections.gloss_en: שרא ליה מריה לגניבא -- השתא צואה, אמר רב יהודה אמר רב כיון שקרמו פניה מותר, מי רגלים מיבעיא?! if Rav permits crusted feces, he would surely permit urine whose mark alone remains

answered_by.gloss_en: מאי חזית דסמכת אהא, סמוך אהא -- Rabba bar Rav Huna in Rav's name: feces even like earthenware is forbidden (= p_kecheres_asura), so the premise is not secure

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי... מאי לאו נבלעו דומיא דיבשו: as dried means its mark is not visible, so absorbed -- so a visible mark forbids even though it no longer moistens!

answered_by.gloss_en: ולטעמיך אימא רישא: כל זמן שמטפיחין הוא דאסור, הא רשומן ניכר שרי! אלא מהא ליכא למשמע מינה -- the two clauses imply opposite things; nothing can be inferred from this baraita
